display.purpose: Scores and the verdict; sized with @ScaledMetric, 28 to 96pt by context.

headline.purpose: The one big statement on a result or ceremony screen.

label.purpose: Section and status labels, in capitals.

motion.name: grow
motion.purpose: Length or possession changing once. Geometry only. The only overshoot.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Anything live that moves or resizes.

motion.name: fade
motion.purpose: Appearance only; what motion becomes under Reduce Motion.

motion.name: late
motion.purpose: Anything that arrives after its cause, such as a spinner.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one pinned action on a screen. Ink, never amber.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: -apple-system, 'SF Pro Display', system-ui, sans-serif; font-stretch: condensed; font-size: 17px; font-weight: 600; width: 100%; min-height: 54px; padding: 12px 18px; border: none; border-radius: 14px; transition: opacity 0.14s ease-out; cursor: pointer; background: #111111; color: #FAFAF7; } .ds-btn-primary:hover, .ds-btn-primary:active { opacity: 0.8; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #111111; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.45; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The alternative action beside or below a primary.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { font-family: -apple-system, 'SF Pro Display', system-ui, sans-serif; font-stretch: condensed; font-size: 17px; font-weight: 600; width: 100%; min-height: 54px; padding: 12px 18px; border: none; border-radius: 14px; transition: opacity 0.14s ease-out; cursor: pointer; background: #E6E6E0; color: #111111; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover, .ds-btn-secondary:active { opacity: 0.8; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #111111; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Quiet Button
components.description: Rare and destructive text actions, such as Sign Out.
components.css: .ds-btn-quiet { font-family: -apple-system, 'SF Pro Display', system-ui, sans-serif; font-stretch: condensed; font-size: 17px; font-weight: 600; width: 100%; min-height: 44px; background: none; border: none; color: #5E5E62; transition: opacity 0.14s ease-out; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-quiet:hover, .ds-btn-quiet:active { opacity: 0.8; } .ds-btn-quiet:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #111111; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Panel
components.description: The raised surface for cards and grouped rows: one tone off the ground, no shadow.
components.css: .ds-panel { font-family: -apple-system, 'SF Pro Display', system-ui, sans-serif; background: #EFEFEA; border-radius: 20px; padding: 0 16px; color: #111111; font-size: 15px; } .ds-panel-row { padding: 16px 0; } .ds-panel-row + .ds-panel-row { border-top: 1px solid #DEDED8; }

components.name: Section Label
components.description: Condensed capital label above a section or as a status.
components.css: .ds-section-label { font-family: -apple-system, 'SF Pro Display', system-ui, sans-serif; font-stretch: condensed; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 1.2px; color: #111111; }

components.name: Score Numerals
components.description: The score: yours in amber, theirs in ink, split by the slash.
components.css: .ds-score { font-family: -apple-system, 'SF Pro Display', system-ui, sans-serif; font-stretch: ultra-condensed; font-size: 56px; font-weight: 800; line-height: 1; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 14px; } .ds-score-you { color: #9C6500; } .ds-score-them { color: #111111; } .ds-score-slash { width: 6px; height: 48px; background: #CFCFC9; transform: skewX(-12deg); }

narrative.overview:
HealthComp looks like the board above an arena. Numbers are the heroes: heavy,
compressed numerals sized to be read across a room, under condensed capital
labels. Everything that is not a number is flat and neutral, a page tone and a
panel tone one step apart, so the board never competes with the score. Colour
is rationed to a single meaning: it is you. Your rings keep Apple's Move,
Exercise and Stand hues; your score, name and wins are amber; your opponent and
every piece of structure are ink and grey.

The mood is sporty and bold. Weight is heavy, edges are firm, type is
condensed, and the mark's 12-degree slash runs through bars, splits and
transitions as the line between you and them.

It is not an Apple Fitness clone: no black field of glowing concentric rings as
the main visual. And it is not licensed fight branding: the title-fight framing
uses original art and wording only, never anything that reads as a real
promotion's graphics.
keyCharacteristics: Heavy compressed score numerals over condensed capital labels.
One accent, amber, and it always means the viewer.
Flat surfaces; depth comes from tone, not shadow.
The 12-degree slash as the recurring divider and the origin of motion.
System typeface only (SF Pro in its compressed and condensed widths).
Light and dark are both first-class; the watch is always dark.

rules.name: The Colour Means You Rule
rules.body: Ring hues and amber are only ever the viewer's own. The opponent and all structure stay neutral. No new colours are added.

rules.name: The Neutral Action Rule
rules.body: Primary buttons are ink, not amber. Colour is not spent on calls to action.

rules.name: The Three Widths Rule
rules.body: Compressed for numbers that are scores, condensed for labels and names, regular for prose. A width is never chosen for looks.

rules.name: The Scaled Score Rule
rules.body: Fixed-size score numerals go through `@ScaledMetric` relative to a text style. No bare point sizes for text.

rules.name: The Flat Board Rule
rules.body: No shadows on everyday screens. Glow and flash are allowed only inside the set pieces: the versus intro, the judges' decision and the belt ceremonies.

dos: Do keep colour for the viewer: ring hues for their rings, amber for their score, name and wins.
Do make the number the largest thing on the screen, in compressed heavy tabular figures.
Do build surfaces from ground, panel and control tones with hairlines.
Do use the Theme tokens, `SectionLabel`, `themePanel` and the three button styles before making a new one.
Do choose motion from the five named animations by what changed.
Do give every moving piece a still state for Reduce Motion.
Do make controls feel tactile and punchy when refining them.
donts: Don't colour an opponent, a status or a button with ring hues or amber.
Don't add a colour that is not in the Theme.
Don't add shadows to everyday screens.
Don't make glowing concentric rings on black the main visual.
Don't use anything that reads as a real fight promotion's graphics, name, logo or catchphrases.
Don't set text in a bare point size.
Don't add a second overshooting curve.
